correctness.rationale: A proper Petersen three-colouring necessarily contains a unique size-four star colour class; after its removal the remaining Petersen induced graph is 3K2, and its two colour classes form one three-star and one triangle. This gives all 5*4*6=120 states. Exactly six Kempe component switches are derived exhaustively from AB=K1+C6, BC=3K2, and AC=a connected 7-vertex tree. The explicit six-rule move graph admits a complete seven-category BFS certificate with distance shells (1,6,25,61,27), and five-label/three-colour relabelling symmetry proves the same shells for all states. Independent direct colouring enumeration and symbolic-state verification were executed from packaged source and agreed on 360 edges, the 20-vertex quotient, radius/diameter four, and the 60 disjoint one-site recolouring edges. This is exact finite exhaustion, not extrapolation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Connectivity in a larger graph class and generic algorithmic complexity theorems do not imply exact 120-vertex adjacency, quotient or distance distributions. Single-vertex recolouring is a different graph: here it produces 60 isolated K2 components whereas component-wise Kempe switching produces the connected diameter-four graph.

originality.rationale: The new item is not the previously known count of 120 named/20 unlabelled Petersen 3-colourings nor the previously proved connectivity of every nonexceptional cubic three-colouring Kempe graph. Its exact six-rule move graph, five four-clique quotient connected by K5 reversals, identical distance shells (1,6,25,61,27), and one-site 60K2 contrast require information absent from those count and connectivity statements. Targeted published-literature and research-record comparisons identified no stated covering result; residual unindexed historical priority risk is retained.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph at its chromatic threshold is a natural canonical benchmark for Kempe dynamics. A simple and complete quotient into five K4 cliques on the directed edges of K5, a uniform exact four-step eccentricity, and the sharp difference between connected Kempe mobility and 60 isolated one-vertex recolouring pairs give substantive structural and metric information beyond counting and connectivity. It is a motivated complete finite classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice; no general theorem or paper-scale extension is claimed.
